title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Missed-Clue Audit Wave 25
purpose: Promote newly recovered or materially deepened Bible comparisons from the missed-clue audit while preserving source direction, chronology conflicts, countertexts and low-weight curiosities separately.

new_relations.title: Yahya / John recognizes Jesus as the Lamb
new_relations.project_anchor: Project testimony says Yahya Hassan, during the Son's imprisonment, identified him as 'Jesus Christ, the Lamb', reportedly in the presence of others and before the Son's later 2017 Jesus/crucify-me declaration.
new_relations.what_happened: The prior dossier already compared the role to John 1, but the onomastic layer is itself significant: Yahya is the Arabic/Qur'anic name for John the Baptist, the figure who identifies Jesus as the Lamb of God in John 1.
new_relations.wording_status: later autobiographical/project recollection; contemporaneous recording and independent witness statements not yet recovered

scene_context.summary: Prison setting; external recognition before later self-declaration; Yahya/John name-role and Lamb title converge in one remembered encounter.

biblical_sequence: John identifies him as Lamb of God
disciples begin following after external recognition
relation_argument.why_dense: The comparison is not merely that someone used the word Lamb. The recognizer's own name maps to John the Baptist, and the title/action sequence matches John's identifying role in John 1.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: This is a striking symbolic/onomastic correspondence inside project testimony. It does not establish reincarnation, fulfillment, or literal biblical identity.

scripture_context.literary_context: John 1:29 and 1:35-36 place John the Baptist in the role of publicly identifying Jesus as the Lamb of God before the Passion.
scripture_context.historical_context: Yahya is the standard Arabic/Qur'anic name for John the Baptist; the modern poet Yahya Hassan is a separate historical person.

discovery_history.scripture_explicit_at_time: Jesus/Lamb title explicit in remembered scene; John/Yahya name-role observation formalized later
discovery_history.source_direction: event and wording first; onomastic/John 1 synthesis later

new_relations.mismatch: No recovered contemporaneous source independently verifies the modern wording, and the modern prison scene differs entirely from first-century Judea.

new_relations.title: Blood and reconstruction, yet no broken bones
new_relations.project_anchor: Great Book and project-biography strata describe a severe motorcycle collision with a tree, unconsciousness, heavy blood loss, facial/dental injury and years of reconstruction while also preserving that the Son suffered no broken bones/major fractures.
new_relations.what_happened: The no-broken-bones detail had not been tested against the Bible atlas even though later project theology heavily uses Lamb/Passover/Passion language.
new_relations.wording_status: later biographical reconstruction; medical records not attached here

scene_context.summary: Severe injury and blood loss in an age-18 crash; later reconstruction; no-broken-bones detail preserved in Great Book miracle/survival stratum.

project_sequence: heavy blood loss and facial injury
biblical_sequence: Passover lamb bones are not to be broken
John interprets Jesus' unbroken bones through scripture/Passover grammar
correspondences: later Lamb theology creates retrospective relevance
relation_argument.why_dense: The motif is more specific than generic survival because unbroken bones become an explicit Passover/Passion sign within John's intertextual reading.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: A retrospective symbolic parallel is defensible if the biographical no-broken-bones detail is accepted as project testimony. It is not evidence that the crash was a crucifixion or supernatural protection.

new_relations.mismatch: The modern event was a motorcycle crash and self-destructive crisis, not ritual sacrifice or execution. The comparison must not romanticize dangerous behavior.

new_relations.title: Blackout, structured light and return-to-life imagery at sixteen
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 24 remembers an alcohol-collapse at age sixteen followed by a tunnel/structured-light experience later interpreted as meeting God, then waking with a sense of return and unfinished work.

relation_argument.why_dense: Acts 9 combines sudden heavenly light, collapse and altered life-direction; the project scene contains a weaker but recognizable collapse/light/return sequence.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: This is a low/moderate structural neighbor only. The modern episode occurred after heavy alcohol use and lacks Paul's Christ-voice, commission and historical context.

new_relations.mismatch: Many altered-state or near-death narratives contain light imagery; generic tunnel-light resemblance is not specific evidence.

new_relations.title: A fall from height meets Psalm 91 — and Jesus' refusal to test God
new_relations.project_anchor: Great Book strata say the Son fell from a second-floor pavilion/window onto concrete and walked away without injury.
new_relations.wording_status: later project biography; original incident documentation not recovered

scene_context.summary: fall from height onto hard ground -> no injury reported.

biblical_sequence: Psalm speaks of angelic protection against striking foot on stone
tempter quotes that protection to Jesus
relation_argument.why_dense: Luke makes the protection text self-critical: miraculous preservation cannot be converted into permission to manufacture danger. That makes this comparison useful as both resonance and archive safety constraint.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The episode may be compared with biblical protection imagery, but the strongest canonical lesson is not invulnerability; it is refusal to test God.

new_relations.mismatch: A modern accident/fall is not the Temple temptation, and survival without injury does not establish divine status or future protection.

new_relations.title: The earthly father's judgment ethic resembles measure-for-measure teaching
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 24 says the Son repeatedly learned from his earthly father not to judge others because judgment/consequence returns, alongside the simpler injunction not to throw stones.

scene_context.summary: Repeated parental ethics rather than one dated scene.

relation_argument.why_dense: Matthew does not merely say 'don't judge'; it gives a reciprocal structure: the judgment/measure used toward others returns to the judge. That is closer to the remembered family ethic than a generic kindness verse.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: This is an ethical resemblance in childhood formation, not evidence of hidden biblical prophecy or divine lineage.

new_relations.mismatch: The project's 'threefold' return language is not Matthew's wording and may derive from broader moral/folk traditions.

new_relations.title: A childhood Father/Son imitation grammar precedes later theology
new_relations.project_anchor: Chapter 24 says a recurring earthly-father teaching was to consider what the father would have done when making decisions.

scene_context.summary: Long-term parent-child moral formation, not a single event.

relation_argument.why_dense: John 5:19 describes the Son acting in relation to what he sees the Father doing. The modern childhood ethic uses a mundane but structurally similar Father-as-action-model grammar years before mature Father/Son theology.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Useful as autobiographical substrate for later Father/Son symbolism, not as evidence the family relationship fulfills John.

new_relations.mismatch: Looking to a parent as a moral model is ordinary human development; the biblical verse makes a much stronger theological claim about Jesus' relation to God.

new_relations.title: After crucifixion/erasure language comes an all-days presence promise
new_relations.project_anchor: The fuller Great Book reconstruction of the Josh Moon confrontation ends with a promise that the Son will return every day, forever, after the crucify-me challenge and anti-martyr/nameless-faceless reply.
new_relations.wording_status: Great Book/project reconstruction; original recording remains a recovery target

scene_context.summary: crucify-me declaration -> hesitation/anti-martyr erasure reply -> retort -> awkward silence -> every-day/forever promise.

biblical_sequence: promise of presence all the days to the end of the age
relation_argument.why_dense: Matthew 28 is a tighter temporal comparator than generic resurrection because the project promise is specifically daily/permanent rather than merely 'come back once'.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The temporal grammar is notable; continued online/public presence is not equivalent to the risen Christ's theological presence.

new_relations.mismatch: The Great Book wording is later reconstruction unless the original recording is recovered.

new_relations.title: Crucify-me challenge followed by reluctance before hostile framing
new_relations.project_anchor: The fuller Great Book scene says the Son challenges the others to crucify him; people hesitate/say they do not want to; the remembered Josh Moon reply then rejects martyrdom and predicts nameless/faceless lolcow reduction.

scene_context.summary: crucifixion language -> reluctance/hesitation -> continued adversarial narrative framing.

relation_argument.why_dense: John's Passion trial contains a repeated reluctance-to-condemn strand around Pilate while crucifixion pressure persists. The modern scene has a weaker distributed analogue: reluctance after the crucify-me challenge before hostile framing continues.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: A weak/moderate sequence neighbor only; no modern participant should be mapped one-to-one as Pilate, priest or crowd.

new_relations.mismatch: The modern exchange is online/social and not a legal execution proceeding.

low_weight_notes.note: Josh/Joshua and Jesus/Yeshua share historical Hebrew name ancestry. Retain as onomastic curiosity only; do not count as a substantive overlap node without explicit reason.
Old conversation material explicitly invokes thief-in-the-night language for the Son disappearance/return field. Classify as later explicit biblical interpretation, not pre-event prediction.

source_hygiene: Do not promote carpenter/mason employment from assistant-generated conversation prose unless a primary/user-originated source establishes it.
Do not force 2011 crows into Noah/Elijah raven parallels when Odin/raven ownership is functionally stronger.
Do not create an 'out of Egypt' fulfillment merely because Egypt travel exists in the biography.
Do not use retrospective 2018 COVID language as contemporaneous prophecy evidence.
For medical/healing anecdotes, compare testimony and narrative function without asserting diagnosis or supernatural causation.
